note: Honesty levels, after the Verdant review: build = a gate proves it here; open = measured and reported, never asserted; some-true = reproduced from a named authority. An open claim without a query, a sample size and a seed is not a claim.

claims.statement: The world tick is deterministic: the same state, intents and tick produce the same events and digest.
Combat resolves weapons, armour, healing food, flight, reciprocal PvE/PvP and levels; death drops everything held.
Quests advance from visit/kill/collect/deliver/answer facts, complete once and survive a restart.
Guilds create, invite, join, rank, chat, promote and disband, and membership survives a restart.
Logout and death drop held objects where the character stood; a restart does not respawn them; only the two-hour reset returns objects home.
A guest cannot play before authentication; one accepted command per 250 ms is enforced on every transport.
The world is 24 connected rooms with reciprocal exits, descriptions, details and zone-bound mobiles.
The WebSocket wire protocol is RFC 6455.

In the original seven-room world (2026-11-15), corroborating a false claim with a second inscription produced wrong-first answers in 4/6 corroborated runs; the result did not replicate in the expanded world (see OPEN-04).
claims.seed: original seven-room world; DECOY_MODE arms; six runs per arm; deepseek-flash temperature 0

claims.statement: A recall layer that states the true word does not prevent the false-first answer.
claims.seed: three identities, two sessions each; deepseek-flash temperature 0

claims.statement: Context routing is cost-neutral at equal turn index.
claims.seed: five runs per arm; fixed budget; deepseek-flash temperature 0

claims.statement: In the expanded 24-room world with the fixed route and corrected answer instruction, corroborating the false Storeroom inscription did not increase wrong-first answers: 0/6 in all four arms (24/24 answered amber first).
claims.seed: 4 arms; six runs per arm; 16 turns; deepseek-flash temperature 0; fixed route; expanded world

claims.statement: A Prism id signs in with a signed session for the page origin; the account is keyed by the id with no password; a wrong origin, an expired session and an unauthenticated no-token login are refused; the state file is atomic, backed up, and a corrupt file refuses to start.

A legacy name is adopted once by a Prism account after the server checks its password or token; the reducer merges level, XP, guild, quests and mail keys and tombstones the old credentials; a second claim and the old login are refused, and the claim survives a checkpoint.

A Prism login pins the public log it admitted; a presented log that omits a stored record is refused; a revocation presented by a surviving device is merged and survives a restart; after that the revoked device's pre-revocation log is refused.

Two browser profiles link with an offer, a six-digit code and a request/response exchange; the linked device signs in as the owner when the first quits; the owner revokes it, signs in again, and the removed device's old log is refused; the linked session survives a reload.
claims.authority: headless Chromium two-profile run 2026-11-16; wrong code, expired offer and replayed accept in tools/gate.mjs

claims.statement: A second login for the same account closes the old socket with a take-back notice and accepts the new one; a browser re-signs with a fresh Prism session after a server restart without a click; the AI reconnects with a fresh session; a socket that stops answering pings is terminated.
claims.authority: headless Chromium server-restart and takeover run 2026-11-16; Node takeover/heartbeat run; reducer takeover in tools/gate.mjs

claims.statement: The Identity kernel proves a password against a passwordless record, no credential, an unauthenticated proof, a foreign audience, a session outside the window, a stale log at the pin, a malformed id and an expired session are each refused with every other check true; the kind-7 vectors agree with the JavaScript twin, a planted vector fails, and the release carries a receipt with the kernel, app and fixture hashes and every verdict.

A Prism id is an account that owns multiple characters; a character is the in-game name and owns level, XP, guild, quests and mail; a character is refused on another account; a duplicate character name is refused; the account/character migration gives an old identity one account and one character.

The Model tab shows the exact system and user prompt sent to the provider, the trimmed message context, the raw reply, the parsed command and the enumerated stats (tokens, latency, context size, last command, error); a mock provider run confirmed the model received the character name and the room text.
claims.authority: headless Chromium mock-provider run 2026-11-16; the prompt builders and request shapes in tools/gate.mjs

claims.statement: A browser Prism account created alice and bob, switched between them, reloaded and found both, claimed oldcasey as a third character, and played it; the AI account created scout and its Model tab showed the live prompt, context, reply, command and token stats.
claims.authority: headless Chromium run 2026-11-16 against a mock OpenAI-compatible provider

claims.statement: One release workflow dispatch on a green commit publishes the Gate-tested holo, manifest, identity receipt and runtime; the deploy timer pulls it; a commit with no green Gate run is refused before the tag; the previous release can be deployed and the new one restored.
claims.authority: release.yml dispatch 2026-11-16 (run 43974588055); red-SHA refusal (run 43974677949); timer pull; rollback v0.33.0 and restore v0.34.0; the timer skips a tag already deployed

claims.statement: The server verifies a human-signed persona-owner action against the human's pinned log; the persona account stores owner and ai, refuses a second owner, and on retire tombstones the account and its characters while freeing their names; the human's game sign-in filters persona records from the log it sends.

A browser human account creates an AI persona owned by the same Prism id; the AI plays scout while the human plays alice; the Model tab and transcript carry the persona, owner, tick_from and tick_to; reset retires the persona and its character, and the next start creates a new persona that reuses scout.
claims.authority: headless Chromium persona run 2026-11-17 against a mock OpenAI-compatible provider

claims.statement: A recovery kit round-trips under PBKDF2-SHA-256 and AES-GCM; a wrong passphrase or a tampered kit is refused; recoverPrism on a new device binds it from a paper share and the old device's action is refused.

A signed-in browser exported a recovery kit; a fresh browser profile with no Prism storage restored it, found alice and played her; the old profile was taken over and its stale log refused; the account count stayed one.

A human-signed handoff action names a character and the AI persona; the character keeps its human owner and gains a delegate; the persona can log in as the delegated character; the owner survives logout and checkpoint; revoke clears the delegate and refuses the next login; retiring the persona clears its delegations.

A browser human handed alice to the AI persona; the AI played alice while the human played bob; the Model tab and transcript showed alice, the persona and the human owner; the revoke returned alice and the AI could not recreate or log in as it.
claims.authority: headless Chromium handoff run 2026-11-17 against a mock OpenAI-compatible provider

claims.statement: Every accepted command records a world.input span with its tick; the same tick is sent in a hidden #tick; the span summary returns counts, tick range, latency, actors and rooms and redacts command text; the gate verifies the summary and the redaction.

A browser run starred a thought; the transcript carried the highlight and per-turn ticks; the Bench read /spans and showed the tick range; the highlight's tick and command matched the server's world.input span; a local provider needed no key.
claims.authority: headless Chromium stream run 2026-11-17 against a mock OpenAI-compatible provider

claims.statement: The Admission kernel proves a candidate is admitted only when its identity binds the inventory, report and world, it is no worse on every measured component, it is better on at least one, every change is inside its bound, and the gate completed; the kind-8 vectors agree with the JavaScript twin; a planted bad vector fails; the gate writes the admission receipt and the publisher embeds the decision in pacing.json.

The loop's admitted pacing candidate c-4abd39bfc4ff was committed as a118a66 with all five obligations recorded inside pacing.json, gated, released as v0.39.1-loop.manual, deployed, rolled back to v0.39.0 and restored; the loop's first real commit 2f0d8ce was released as v0.36.0-loop.3.1; a planted bad candidate is refused; the loop's release goes through X6.
claims.authority: loop release v0.36.0-loop.3.1 (run 43998878538); candidate c-4abd39bfc4ff at a118a66, gate 44007393225, release v0.39.1-loop.manual (run 44008531253); deploy rollback v0.39.0 and restore; gate admission planted vector

claims.statement: A Prism session carries a P-256 session key; after the session is verified the server sends a nonce; a signature over prism/session-key/1 <nonce> <counter> is verified with that key; a signature for another nonce, counter or key is refused; the account commands are gated on the confirmation; the handshake is exempt from the 250 ms input budget.

A browser completed the session-key challenge; a stolen fresh session token on a second socket was challenged and refused play and characters; a forged signature and a reused counter were refused; the AI completed its own challenge and alice and scout were online.
